Walmart on Thursday reported earnings and revenue that narrowly topped estimates and raised its full-year outlook as it saw strong e-commerce growth ahead of the busy holiday season.

Recent findings suggest that walmart said global e-commerce sales surged 17% in the fiscal third quarter, driven by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery, with Walmart U.S. up 23% and Sam's Club U.S. rising 30%. Its Walmart U.S. advertising business saw a 37% sales increase for the quarter.

Walmart stated it rolled back prices on nearly 8,000 products across its stores, a focus as U.S. consumers worry about the cost of living in the face of elevated food and gas prices.

CEO John Furner told CNBC's Becky Quick that the company has seen higher-than-expected diesel costs, but that tariff refunds have helped the retailer to offset those inputs and maintain lower prices.

It has been revealed that "The reality is that increases in diesel fuel and transportation, they do work their way into cost of goods," Furner said in an exclusive interview. "So we're hoping to see these costs come down as soon as possible, and we'll keep prices as low as we can.".

CFO John David Rainey told CNBC that growth in online orders for Walmart and Sam's Club was driven by an emphasis on speed of delivery and reduced prices. He added that Walmart saw its largest share gains in the food category in three years during the third quarter.

It has been revealed that "This was another really solid quarter for us, we feel good about it," Rainey told CNBC. "We continue to gain share while continuing to improve the profitability of our digital businesses.".

Recent findings suggest that walmart also raised its full-year guidance, now expecting net sales to increase between 4.9% and 5.2%, compared with previous guidance of a 4% to 5% increase. Rainey stated Walmart is maintaining "flexibility" in its guidance.

Sources indicate that walmart anticipates adjusted earnings per share will come in between $2.84 and $2.89, compared with a prior range of $2.80 to $2.87. It's also now expecting adjusted operating income to increase between 8% and 8.6%, up from the previous outlook of between 7% and 8.5% growth.

Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

In a recent development, for the quarter ended Oct. 31, the company reported net income of $4.95 billion, or 62 cents per share, down from $6.14 billion, or 77 cents per share, a year earlier. Revenue rose 5.2%.

Adjusting for investment gains and losses, tax matters and reorganization charges, Walmart earned 65 cents per share.

Walmart U.S. recorded net sales of $125 billion, up 3.6% from a year earlier. Its comparable sales excluding fuel rose 2.9%, in line with Wall Street expectations, according to StreetAccount.

Industry observers note that furner also said Walmart is seeing encouraging adoption of its artificial intelligence agent, named Sparky, especially ahead of the holiday season. He said it's led to customer basket increases of 40% on average.

"It just is a great way of just completing the entire basket and solving entire the solution for people," he said.

It has been revealed that sam's Club reported net sales of $25.9 billion, marking a 10% increase from the year-ago period. It said its sales were driven by strength in the grocery category and general merchandise.

Industry observers note that in October, Walmart announced it was launching a joint membership option with Walmart+ and Sam's Club as it leans further into convenience. Both stores will still offer stand-alone memberships, as well.

According to recent reports, furner told CNBC the new membership has brought roughly 2 million new people into Sam's Club since its launch in late October. Though the manufacturer reimbursed some members for the new membership rate, Rainey added that it's already seeing positive returns on the joint model and that consumers are "spending appreciably more.".

The company on Thursday mentioned its global membership fee revenue grew 17% in the third quarter.

The manufacturer is typically well insulated from macroeconomic pressures because of its value reputation. Last quarter, the company said it was lowering prices of products across multiple categories, including beef.

Rainey said Thursday that he's "optimistic" about consumer spending heading into the holiday season and that the fourth quarter is already "off to a pretty good start.".

The big-box retailer has posted solid growth over the past few quarters as it sees customers gravitate to reduced prices, improvements in delivery and gains in its advertising business. It's also leaned into attracting higher-income consumers with its Walmart+ membership.

Shares of Walmart have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year to date.

Joining the film as executive producers, the two Mexican icons’ support will galvanise the film’s campaign for Academy Award live action short film recognition.

Chief International Correspondent.

Salma Hayek Pinault and boxing world champion Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez two of Mexico’s greatest contemporary icons, have boarded Cannes 2026 short film Palme d’Or winner “For the Opponents” as executive producers galvanizing Mexico’s push for the film’s contention in the Academy Award Live Action Short Film race.

“For the Opponents” (“Para los Contrincantes”) has already grabbed a lot of attention as the Cannes Official Selection conquering follow-up to Argentine writer-director Federico Luis’ “Simon of the Mountain,” his first solo feature and a Cannes Critics’ Week Grand Prize in 2024. Related Stories As Russell Brand’s Begins a 10-Year Prison Sentence, Why Celebrities Fear the Power of an Exposé Conspiracy Thriller 'The Awakening,' Starring Kevin Spacey, Gets U.S. Release (EXCLUSIVE).

Hayek and Canelo’s support, however, will now take media and Academy notice to another level.

Industry observers note that starring the young Damián López and shot in 16mm and a 4:3 box format, “For the Opponents” trails Damian, a young boy, as he is registered for a child boxing match by his father coach. It then takes in four rounds of combat, with dad’s instructions heard off-screen– If you open your mouth they could fracture your jaw,” “hold your hands up,” “throw two punches to the chest, then jabs to he head” as he also pressures Damián by way of encouragement: “This is the chance of your life,” he is heard saying.

According to recent reports, damián only states two words in the whole film – “Thank you” to the check-in registrar. Yet Luis’ while focus is on him, as he boxes and is caught in close-up listening to his father, facing the judges’ verdict and reacting to that with a welter of mixed emotions.

Luis’ direction is notable for its contention and detail, both physical and psychological. There is no sensationalism, though respect, for the plucky Damián and no “poverty porn” in a scene afterwards of Damián and a friend running down a street in Mexico City’s Tepito district, sometimes reduced by descriptions to just one of the City’s most dangerous no-go hoods.

In a recent development, “As an executive producer, I couldn’t be prouder to support this remarkable short film. ‘For the Opponents’ is deeply affecting and seeing young Damián’s grit and determination has stuck with me. I am heartbroken feeling the pain in his fight for himself and for his family,” stated Salma Hayek Pinault, Oscar nominated for her performance in “Frida” and one of Hollywood’s most influential Latina voices.

Industry observers note that “When I saw Damián in the gym, I saw myself as a boy. I also started very young, with a pair of gloves and the dream of becoming a champion. This film moved me because behind the boxer there is a child, with his dreams and his emotions. I’m very proud to support a story that indicates such a real side of Mexican boxing,” noted ‘Canelo’ Álvarez, a four division boxing world champion.

In his most recent fight, held Oct. 31 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, ‘Canelo’ Álvarez scored a unanimous decision victory over France’s previously undefeated Christian Mbilli to reclaim the WBC super middleweight world title. It is his 22nd world championship victory.

Sold by Luxbox, “For the Opponents” is backed by a prestige producer package of Chile’s Planta (“La Perra,”“Double Freedom”), Mexico’s Cárcava Cine (“The Garden We Dreamed”) Fiasco (“Hijas del Bosque”), Deptford Film (“Double Freedom”) and Les Films du Worso (“Dao”).

Sources indicate that fernando Bascuñán, Fernanda de la Peza, Elena Fortes and Augusto Matte produce. Héctor Sulaimán serves as executive producers and Sylvie Plait and Alejandro Arenas as co-producers.

The film “explores the dreams, expectations and family bonds surrounding a child trying to make his way in the sport,” the producers said in a statement.

“For the Opponents” has been selected for more than 50 international festivals including Telluride, San Sebastián and Tallinn Black Nights.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO signals that the chipmaker may have grown too crucial to the stock market for the US government to hold it accountable for national security lapses, intelligence and export-control experts warn WIRED.
  • Recent findings suggest that nvidia’s board brought back Huang on Monday, 11 days after he resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs—one of them with Alice Huang, a woman US intelligence suspects has ties to China’s Ministry of State Security.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO signals that the chipmaker may have grown too crucial to the stock market for the US government to hold it accountable for national security lapses, intelligence and export-control experts warn WIRED. The move also undercuts the warnings Washington routinely issues to American companies and foreign governments about Beijing’s pursuit of US technology, they say.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia’s board brought back Huang on Monday, 11 days after he resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs—one of them with Alice Huang, a woman US intelligence suspects has ties to China’s Ministry of State Security. The board stated input from “senior levels of the United States government” left it confident that his return poses no national security risk.

President Donald Trump told The Wall Street Journal he lobbied the board directly and through intermediaries, and that Nvidia’s falling share price helped his case. The board acted before its own investigation of Huang had concluded, and while the Justice Department is pursuing a criminal probe of Megaspeed—a Singapore organization Alice Huang once ran—over the alleged diversion of Nvidia chips to China. Alice Huang is also under investigation, according to director of national intelligence Jay Clayton.

Industry observers note that the experts tell WIRED they worry more about the precedent Huang’s return sets than about Huang himself. Some say the scrutiny now on him makes further compromise unlikely. But Beijing may already have gained insight into Nvidia’s chip designs and its private conversations with the White House and Congress, or, through Megaspeed, obtained the chips themselves, they say, and no one has publicly established what, if anything, it got.

Sources indicate that several want to know who gave the board its assurances and on what basis, and whether the government ran a counterintelligence damage assessment or simply made a political judgment. They also say the administration has repeatedly failed to enforce its own export controls, and that when intelligence concerns appear to yield to market pressure, US warnings about China start to sound negotiable, to Beijing’s benefit.

Recent findings suggest that “If intelligence assessments are seen to be overridden, selectively interpreted, or publicly dismissed for political or commercial reasons, this could undermine long-term confidence in the independence of national security institutions,” states Tahlia Peterson, a cyber and technology research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute, a London defense think tank. “That would be damaging to US national security, and potentially advantageous to Beijing.”.

Advisers briefed Trump at least twice on Alice Huang’s links to Chinese intelligence before the affair became public, and both times he played down their concerns, The Upcoming York Times reported Sunday. When the Journal asked him on Monday about Republican lawmakers who say Huang’s return endangers national security, Trump pointed to Nvidia’s rebounding stock.

Recent findings suggest that “Some tech companies have become so big—and so important to the stock market—that Washington is reluctant to hold them accountable for national security lapses,” notes Edward Fishman, director of the Council on Foreign Relations’ Maurice R. Greenberg Center for Geoeconomics.

Fishman sees a parallel in Wall Street’s slow reckoning with sanctions. “It took years of aggressive enforcement to get banks to take US sanctions compliance seriously,” he indicates. “We haven’t seen anything comparable in the tech sector, which helps explain why US export controls remain so weak and leaky.” Reinstating Huang on the administration's assurances before Nvidia’s own investigation has concluded “does not inspire confidence that meaningful enforcement is coming,” he says.

Emily Kilcrease, a former deputy assistant US trade representative who now directs the Energy, Economics, and Security program at the Center for a Upcoming American Security, indicates the administration’s record gives little reason to take those assurances at face value. “We cannot rely on the administration’s judgment, as it has repeatedly failed to enforce export controls over the past year,” she says.

It has been revealed that on Monday, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist, and the administration has recently moved to tighten rules on China’s AI industry. But Kilcrease says it acted only under pressure. “Given the poor track record on export controls and their broader accommodationist stance toward China, it’s fair to ask whether they are willing to really enforce the new controls,” she says.

It has been revealed that the board’s assurances appear to have come mostly from the Justice Department. Attorney general Todd Blanche allegedly told Trump and vice president JD Vance on Saturday that Huang was neither a target nor a subject of any department investigation, and that the department had no evidence he had broken the law or posed a national security risk, the Journal reports. Vance then reportedly sought assurances for the board that the administration did not consider Huang a threat and that he would not face criminal charges. Trump told the Times he also consulted Clayton before pushing for Huang’s return. (“I can’t do this and then all of a sudden have somebody get indicted,” he stated.).

Nvidia did not immediately respond to WIRED’s request for comment.

Whether Huang broke any laws is a separate question from whether Beijing gained anything through him. “Did [the assurances] reflect a counterintelligence damage assessment by the intelligence community or the FBI, or were they political in nature?” says Jessica Brandt, a senior fellow for technology and national security at the Council on Foreign Relations who previously directed the Foreign Malign Influence Center at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence. “Lawmakers should press on that.”.

In a recent development, senior officials may have seen intelligence that isn’t public, so the assurances shouldn’t just be dismissed, notes Sunny Cheung, a China studies fellow at the Jamestown Foundation. “However, we still don’t know who provided those assurances, what evidence they reviewed, or how they reached their conclusion, particularly when Nvidia’s own independent investigation remains unfinished,” he says.

Lawmakers appear to have seen little of that evidence. At a briefing this month by CIA director John Ratcliffe and Clayton that was scheduled to cover Iran, lawmakers pressed for answers about Huang, and the responses left some of them puzzled, according to the Times. A follow-up briefing for senior national security staff was postponed.

Cheung notes the Ministry of State Security may not have needed Nvidia’s secrets to profit from the relationship. “From a counterintelligence perspective, I think people are too focused on whether Jensen handed over trade secrets,” he says. “China’s Ministry of State Security wouldn’t necessarily need Nvidia’s next-generation chip blueprints to benefit from access to him.” Insight into Huang’s direct conversations with the president, senior officials, and other top tech executives, along with his views on China and Taiwan and his role in Washington’s export-control debate, “could already be extremely valuable to Beijing,” he says.

Brandt sees the same mix of risks. “Information about Nvidia’s proprietary chip designs could help China advance its own chip design efforts,” she says. “Insight into Nvidia’s conversations with the White House and Congress could help Beijing anticipate where US export control policy is headed.” Investigators should also ask whether Alice Huang compromised Huang’s devices, what security clearance he held, and whether he still holds it, she says.

Sources indicate that huang successfully lobbied the Trump administration to roll back restrictions on Nvidia’s chip sales to China and negotiated a deal giving the US government a 25 percent cut of sales of certain chips approved for export there, the Times has reported. In April, minister of state security Chen Yixin made overcoming the “blockades” that limit China’s access to key technologies like AI a sixth core mission for his ministry, known as the MSS. Alice Huang’s network of chip-buying companies “lines up precisely” with that mission, Matt Pottinger, who served as deputy national security adviser during Trump’s first term, told the paper.

“A further question is whether Alice Huang was tasked by Chinese intelligence to influence Jensen Huang's views or approach to US export restrictions on China, and, if so, to what extent she succeeded,” Peterson claims. The Journal also reported that the intelligence is inconclusive on whether she was actively tasked to collect information on Huang, and Cheung says “whether any such information was obtained or influence exercised remains unproven.”.

Megaspeed’s purchases are better documented. A Malaysian subsidiary bought at least $4.8 billion worth of equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, according to trade records the Times reviewed. Its subsidiaries have also served Chinese clients, including Alibaba. US intelligence indicates that Alice Huang was in contact with an MSS officer from spring 2025 until this fall, and that her business partner, Kang Wei, also worked with the agency, the paper reported Sunday. Her network has been linked to efforts to supply Nvidia chips to China’s state-owned military contractors. Enough has been reported to suggest that Huang, “wittingly or not, may have played a role in helping Megaspeed as it sought access to advanced Nvidia chips,” Kilcrease indicates.

Megaspeed did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Nicholas Eftimiades, a former CIA and Defense Intelligence Agency officer who teaches homeland security at Penn State Harrisburg, notes Huang himself poses no security risk. Now that the relationship is public, he says, Huang has little chance of unwittingly passing along more information about US government policy or Nvidia’s board deliberations. Peterson agrees that scrutiny from Nvidia’s board, its compliance staff, federal agencies, and Congress likely limits any further exposure. But “we are still in the dark as to whether any sensitive information may already have been compromised,” she says, “or whether any resulting harm can be identified or mitigated.”.

Recent findings suggest that huang’s defenders have repeatedly noted that he never received a defensive briefing, a warning the government sometimes gives Americans whom foreign intelligence services target. Nvidia’s board indicates its investigation will continue with Huang’s cooperation, and the company is searching for a chief compliance officer. A committee of independent directors is examining whether Huang shared corporate or national security information with Alice Huang. The board has also formed a new committee of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

It has been revealed that peterson indicates the company’s leadership matters. “Nvidia is an exceptionally notable company, and there are legitimate arguments about the implications of losing its leadership at a critical moment in the global AI race,” she says. “But those considerations should not determine the conclusions of national security investigations.”.

Recent findings suggest that trump told CNBC Monday that keeping the United States ahead of China made reinstating Huang imperative. “If we didn't do this, I could see China coming in and saying to Jensen, ‘Hey, how would you like to come to China?’” he said.

For Brandt, the bigger cost may come with Washington’s next warning. “This erodes the credibility of US government warnings about China’s technological ambitions and how far it will go to achieve them,” she indicates. “How will those warnings land going forward, both with our own companies and with foreign governments? We risk making a hard problem harder: emboldening Beijing while weakening our own defenses.”.

It has been revealed that that cost extends to the allies Washington depends on to police its controls, adds Sarah Bauerle Danzman, an associate professor of international studies at Indiana University’s Hamilton Lugar School. The Commerce Department has few enforcement agents abroad to monitor transshipment, she says, so the system relies on partner countries to run checks and share information about problematic buyers. Singapore says it repeatedly raised concerns with US authorities in this case.

“These types of incidents make such cooperation more difficult to sustain,” Bauerle Danzman says.

Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter have agreed to closed-door, transcribed interviews with three House committees on December 1 and 2. “The legal and reputational risk of hiring a CEO who may very well be convicted in the United States or other nations of violating espionage and export control laws is now [borne] by the board of Nvidia, but the national security risk is passed along to the United States military and its citizens,” Senator Kevin Cramer, a North Dakota Republican, said on X.

Sources indicate that “I think Congress has gotten fed up,” indicates Kilcrease, who cites bipartisan concern about Megaspeed and what she calls the administration’s broader accommodation of China. “We can expect hearings and investigations from multiple committees, and Congress is highly motivated to pass legislation to tighten export controls, increase its oversight of administration decisions, and bolster enforcement.”.

Industry observers note that “Jensen may be back, and he should not be presumed guilty of wrongdoing,” Cheung indicates. “But his reinstatement should not be mistaken for a clean bill of health. Nvidia and the administration still have important questions to answer.”.

Ancient rocks from the Moon’s far side rewrite the Solar System’s violent past

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ancient rocks collected from the Moon's far side are revealing newly introduced details about the violent events that shaped the early Solar System.
  • Recent findings suggest that newly introduced research suggests that the intense asteroid bombardment experienced by the Moon did not occur primarily during a single, catastrophic period, as scientists previously believed.
  • Industry observers note that the Moon offers a rare opportunity to investigate this distant past.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ancient rocks collected from the Moon's far side are revealing newly introduced details about the violent events that shaped the early Solar System. The discoveries are challenging a scientific theory that has stood for decades and could also provide key clues about the conditions that influenced Earth's earliest history.

Recent findings suggest that newly introduced research suggests that the intense asteroid bombardment experienced by the Moon did not occur primarily during a single, catastrophic period, as scientists previously believed. Instead, evidence preserved in lunar rocks indicates that the frequency of these collisions decreased gradually over billions of years.

Industry observers note that the Moon offers a rare opportunity to investigate this distant past. While erosion, volcanic activity, and the movement of tectonic plates have destroyed much of Earth's earliest geological record, the lunar surface has retained evidence of ancient asteroid impacts dating back billions of years.

Why the Moon's Far Side Holds Important Clues.

Dr. Fred Jourdan, a research co-author affiliated with Curtin University's School of Earth and Planetary Sciences and John de Laeter Centre, explained that lunar rocks preserve valuable information about the Solar System's earliest history. These natural records allow researchers to investigate events that took place soon after the planets formed.

Industry observers note that "The Moon is like a time capsule -- it has preserved a record of events that have been erased from Earth by erosion, plate tectonics and other geological processes," Dr. Jourdan noted.

Recent findings suggest that "Samples collected from the Moon's far side are particularly significant because they allow us to compare two very different parts of the Moon for the first time. Until now, almost everything we knew came from the side facing Earth.".

"By analyzing these ancient rocks, we can better understand when major asteroid impacts occurred and how the early Solar System evolved. The far side preserves a cleaner record of those earliest impacts because it was much less affected by later geological events than the side facing Earth.

"These samples are helping us rewrite parts of the Moon's history and suggest the early Solar System experienced a long decline in asteroid impacts rather than a single catastrophic bombardment.".

Reconstructing Billions of Years of Asteroid Impacts.

According to recent reports, to investigate the Moon's bombardment history, the researchers examined tiny pieces of lunar rock for evidence of ancient collisions. Their analysis identified impact events dating from approximately 4.33 billion to 1.13 billion years ago, providing a record that spans more than three billion years.

Recent findings suggest that these findings offer a newly introduced perspective on how asteroid impacts changed over time. Rather than supporting the idea of a relatively brief period of exceptionally intense bombardment, the evidence points to a much longer process in which impacts became progressively less frequent.

The implications extend beyond the Moon itself. According to Dr. Jourdan, reconstructing the history of lunar impacts can help scientists better understand the events that affected Earth during its earliest stages of development.

What Ancient Moon Rocks Reveal About Early Earth.

"The Moon and Earth share a common history, but the evidence of early impacts has largely disappeared from our planet," Dr. Jourdan mentioned.

"Because the Earth and Moon formed together, every major impact recorded on the Moon tells us something about the conditions experienced by the young Earth.

"Studying lunar rocks allows us to look back billions of years and better understand the events that shaped the environments of both worlds and helps us understand the role asteroid impacts played in planetary evolution and the conditions that may have influenced the emergence of life on Earth.

"The findings come amid a latest era of lunar exploration and science, with China's Chang'e-6 mission being the first to return samples from the Moon's far side.".

Industry observers note that the return of material from the lunar far side has given scientists an unprecedented opportunity to examine a region that was previously inaccessible to direct sampling. By comparing these rocks with samples from the Moon's near side, researchers can develop a more complete picture of the impacts that shaped the lunar surface and the wider Solar System.

The research was led by the State Key Laboratory of Deep Earth Processes and Resources at the Guangzhou Institute of Geochemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

The findings were published in Science Advances in a paper titled 'The bombardment history on the lunar farside revealed by 40Ar/39Ar geochronology of Chang'e-6 impact melt rocks'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that near the end of Clashing Through the Snow, Michelle Randolph‘s Hannah Hendricks walks past an Eloise portrait in a Upcoming York hotel lobby.
  • “It really choked me up, even as I was walking through the shot,” Young tells The Hollywood Reporter.
  • In a recent development, the moment felt “spiritually correct” for the rising director, who recalls dressing as Kay Thompson’s Eloise for her fourth-grade book day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that near the end of Clashing Through the Snow, Michelle Randolph‘s Hannah Hendricks walks past an Eloise portrait in a Upcoming York hotel lobby. Standing beside it, holding her then seven-month-old daughter, is the film’s director, Carlson Young.

“It really choked me up, even as I was walking through the shot,” Young tells The Hollywood Reporter.

In a recent development, the moment felt “spiritually correct” for the rising director, who recalls dressing as Kay Thompson’s Eloise for her fourth-grade book day. Filming it with her baby on her hip gave her “this kind of out-of-body experience, overlapping-reality thing” that she felt “a lot of little girls could relate to.” Related Stories TV How Amin Joseph Brought "Humanity" to Sonny Liston in 'The Greatest' TV How 'Landman' Star Michelle Randolph Found Love ... In a Rental Car.

It’s a heartwarming moment in a heartwarming movie, and perhaps a surprising film for a director who calls herself a “horror girly.”.

In a recent development, before moving behind the camera, Young built her career as an actor, with credits including Key & Peele, a guest role on Netflix’s Emily in Paris and the 2014 comedy Premature. Her breakout came as Brooke Maddox on MTV’s Scream, the 2015 TV series adaptation of the horror film franchise created by Kevin Williamson and directed by Wes Craven, and Young credits the horror genre with making her want to tell stories in the first place.

“When I was a little girl, horror got me out of bed in the morning. Those are the directors I watched as a kid that made me want to be a director and a storyteller.”.

Having worked with “incredible horror directors on Scream,” Young became fascinated by “what fear has to teach us,” and that curiosity guides her work as a director, even in romance. Her horror “sensibility and natural instinct,” she says, allow her to “clearly identify, in any given scene, where the psychic predator actually is.”.

Years later, Young has directed Prime Video‘s latest cozy holiday rom-com, with snowstorms, rental cars, a bus full of elderly passenger, bookstores and enemies-to-lovers banter, and she claims those horror instincts and her love for nostalgic romances are exactly what helped her find its heart.

“I didn’t necessarily think my next movie would be a holiday rom-com, but I fell in love with the script,” she tells THR. “It reminded me of so many classic holiday rom-coms that I’m nostalgic for.”.

It has been revealed that clashing Through the Snow, which debuted on Prime Video on Monday, stars Landman’s Michelle Randolph and The Summer I Turned Pretty breakout Chris Briney as Hannah Hendricks and Ryan Mitchell, rival book editors competing for a career-saving publishing deal. When their flight is canceled, the pair are forced to share a rental car to New York City in the middle of a holiday snowstorm, each determined to close the deal first. And of course chaos ensues with the holiday journey anything but jolly.

Recent findings suggest that the film, which can also serve as a love letter to books and reading, was pitched as a Planes, Trains and Automobiles for a latest generation, a comparison Young says she had to shed “right off the bat” or risk being overwhelmed by anxiety. Still, she found her film’s driving force in the heart of the 1987 road-trip comedy: the moment John Candy’s Del Griffith tells Steve Martin’s Neal Page, “I like me.”.

In Clashing Through the Snow, that heart comes in a vulnerable motel-room conversation in which Ryan tells Hannah she’s “living a when-then life.” The line spoke personally to Young and became the foundation for the film’s long, funny and often chaotic journey.

“It resonated with me deeply, and I felt like it’s in the zeitgeist. So yes, it’s a comedy of errors, hijinks ensue, it’s a very fun movie, but it does have something to say as well,” Young says. “I did try to do our own version — pay homage to the classic holiday movies that we come back to every year and try to do something new.”.

Clashing Through the Snow may be her newest film, but it also marks a milestone for the director, who kept a “when-then” promise of her own.

“I told myself, ‘When I direct three movies, then I can have a baby.’ And that’s actually what happened,” she indicates. “It’s really cool to bring my daughter into a world where I’m able to do what I’m passionate about and have her by my side. What could be more beautiful than that?”.

Young was on the sunny beaches of Mallorca, Spain, wrapping production on Prime Video’s romantic drama The Last Sunrise when she set her sights on Clashing. She would trade a sun-soaked summer romance for a snowy, cross-country road trip that takes place during the holiday season. And though she was already attached to direct, she still needed the right home for it.

It has been revealed that she had already worked with Amazon on the 2024 romance Upgraded, starring Camila Mendes, and on The Last Sunrise, with Maia Reffico, Fernando Lindez and Eva Longoria, which was then still forthcoming (it debuted in July 2026). For Clashing, her third film with Amazon, she again found a partner in the streamer.

“It made sense, and it’s a movie I really believed in and knew would be great there with the team at Amazon,” Young claims of bringing the film to Prime Video.

With two films out on Prime Video this year, Young has come a long way from her directorial debut, the short film The Blazing World, which premiered at the 2018 Sundance Film Festival. Since then she has directed the 2021 feature-length version of The Blazing World; Upgraded, which has a confirmed sequel; and the survival thriller Trust, starring Sophie Turner.

And while her turn as fan favorite Brooke Maddox in MTV’s iteration of the iconic horror franchise catered to her love for horror, Clashing and its exploration of “living a when-then life” made for a personal, art-imitating-life moment for the director.

Recent findings suggest that “I catch myself in that pattern almost constantly — this natural withholding of, ‘I have to accomplish this before I can give myself this.’ I think that’s very reflective of the world we live in, with the overstimulation and the high speed. We live in overdrive, so it’s something I deal with in real time,” she says.

“From a career perspective, I hope to be able to look back at the end of my life and feel meaning in the work I’ve done. I try really hard with every movie I direct to weave in the medicine I’m capable of reflecting at the time.”.

With The Last Sunrise and now Clashing Through the Snow, the films have marked breakout moments for their leading stars. The Last Sunrise marked Lindez’s first English-language role, while Clashing is Randolph and Briney’s first foray as leading rom-com stars.

Having come up as an actor first, Young has found a kinship in directing talent amid these moments in their journey.

“I understand how vulnerable it is to be an actor. I think that’s a really important thing for directors to be sensitive to — and to know that actors also have incredible ideas. So I love to let whoever I’m working with play, and having been an actress first informs so much of what I do.”.

And how does acting inform her directing? She approaches it from a “different altitude.”.

“I don’t read a script anymore and think, ‘Oh wow, I’d really like to play this character.’ I read a script now with this bird’s-eye view. I feel much more spider-like, weaving different stories and characters together. But I’m actor-first, character-first, so it informs every decision I make as a director.”.

Briney is a talent she predicts “has a long career ahead of him, with many places to go and explore.”.

“I felt like seeing him in a more comedic role would be something incredibly fresh for him. When I met him and spoke to him, it was very obvious that he could do that, so I was really excited to find this character with him. He’s a very charming human, and he’s kind and resourceful. We got to have a lot of fun on set — I would just pitch him jokes and he would land them. He has a real comedic flexibility that I think is super fresh in his generation of actors,” she states.

As for Randolph, Young was struck by the “charm and warmth that she exudes.”.

“She just has this effortless charm of the ’90s and 2000s rom-coms that I think we’re all so nostalgic for.”.

Young says of pairing them, “They’re both incredibly charming and talented actors in their own right, so it’s a dream to put those two together.”.

In addition to Briney and Randolph, the film features a host of familiar faces, including Julia Fox, Andrew Schulz, Lucas Gage, Jake Shane, Tan France, Zarna Garg and even Paris Hilton. Young laughs when it’s suggested the internet indicated up for the road trip.

“You took the words right out of my mouth. The internet is showing up for this road trip,” she claims. “This movie is for the chronically online.”.

In a recent development, each brought the kind of levity the story needed, she says, and the known faces give the audience a familiarity “that feels like a warm hug. You kind of know this person; you’re aware of the energy they bring. It was a really fun recipe. It’s like a cake of the internet.”.

Sources indicate that as for Hilton, who shares a comedic exchange with Briney’s Ryan at one point in the film, Young explains that the randomness of her guest role made the rivalry between Ryan and Hannah even more fun. “We were like, who is a person Ryan could interface with at the Bianca Hart show who would make Hannah go, ‘How the fuck do you — what is going on here?’ She’s so iconic in her own right, and picturing her in that moment made me laugh out loud.”.

Teasing “a lot of exciting projects” on the horizon for next year, Young has one wish as a director: more romance.

“I want to do many more rom-coms. I want to do a lot more romance. At the end of my life, I’d like to look back and be able to see the through line, and I think it continues to reveal itself,” she says. “So far in my career I’ve sailed across different genres, and I’m extremely motivated by asking myself, ‘Why do people like this genre?’ That motivates me to go try to fall in love with it. I’m just trying to understand love, and it takes a trillion forms. We’re specks in the universe in a nanosecond of geological time. There’s a simplicity I like — like a good poem that has to iterate itself over and over again to get to a truly beautiful form.”.

Clashing arrives as onscreen love stories are booming and having now made several of her own, Young believes that “in this digital age we live in, human connection and the intimacy of human relationships are actually kind of novel at this point.

She adds, “As women, we escape into romanticism because there are men and women out there who are able to see you, proverbially, and connect with you at a very deep level — and I think that’s sometimes quite hard to find in the real world. You’re not going to get that from a phone or from the internet. At the end of the day, as a director, I’m seeking that level of intimacy with myself and with the relationships in my life, so I can relate to the audience on that level.”.

In a recent development, “As we continue to evolve as a species, these questions about love and what it means to be vulnerable in a relationship are incredibly notable,” she continues. “Romance and desire are the most interesting things to explore, I think. So it’s not surprising to me at all that there’s a ravenous appetite for it.”.

Going forward, Young also finds great inspiration in “female characters who have a journey to go on.”.

It has been revealed that she explains, “Women are these incredibly complex, raw gems that continue to reveal themselves the more you turn them. So I look for bravery in the characters, and if I can see that, then I can probably carry that torch over the finish line.”.

Though her sights are set on love, would the self-described “horror girly” return to the genre?

Young is open to it but doesn’t want “to chase it.”.

Sources indicate that “I want it to come to me,” she notes. “I don’t know when or where yet, but when I get my horror fangs out, I can’t wait.”.

Clashing Through the Snow is available on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The German government has presented some grim statistics with regard to misogyny, rape, violence and murder, with reported cases of domestic violence at an all-time high.

At a press conference in Berlin on Tuesday, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, Family Affairs Minister Karin Prien and Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig released the latest figures on crimes that specifically target women: whether within families and intimate relationships, in public or online.

In contrast to the statistics pertaining to crime overall, which have remained the same or increased only slightly, reports of crimes against women have increased.

"Behind all these terrible numbers lie individual stories, people and particularly women and girls, whose lives are severely affected by these acts of violence," stated Dobrindt.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In 2025, some 280,000 people were victims of physical abuse in their own homes, a 2.8% increase compared to the previous year. Over 70% of the victims were female. Each hour, 16 women are subjected to physical abuse behind closed doors.

The male victims included boys who had been assaulted by their fathers.

The number of misogynistic hate crimes has also risen dramatically, by almost 50%, to 819 cases.

"The figures show us what it can mean to be a woman in Germany," noted Hubig. "It can mean being killed by one's partner or ex-partner. Being a woman can also mean being physically abused by one's partner or ex-partner in one's own home. Being a woman can mean that one's sexual autonomy is brutally disregarded.".

Sources indicate that according to the latest findings, both perpetrators and victims are getting younger. In 2025, nearly half of all female victims of sexual offenses were under the age of 18. And the number of incidents of online violence against women and girls rose by 15.7%. This includes the unauthorized sharing of videos and photos, verbal abuse, manipulation of images, threats and online blackmail, as well as cyberstalking.

Because many perpetrators and victims are still in their teens, Prien, who is also minister for education, remarked the government wanted to focus primarily on schools, which she explained should become places of prevention.

Sources indicate that "Ultimately, we need to bring about a change in people's mindsets, especially those of men. That will be the deciding factor in the end," she mentioned.

Over the weekend, Justice Minister Hubig had already announced that in future all femicides, the intentional killing of girls and women because of their gender, would be classified as murders. Presently, such crimes are often classified as manslaughter, for which the penalty is less severe than for murder.

Hubig told German broadcaster ZDF that it was increasingly common that femicides be described as family tragedies or as domestic dramas revolving around jealousy and then classified as manslaughter.

Sources indicate that martina Link, the vice president of the Federal Criminal Police Office, was also at the press conference in Berlin. She called for everybody to pay closer attention to the issue, within their own families, neighborhoods or at work.

According to recent reports, "Violence against women is not a private matter," she said. "Not in our immediate surroundings nor in the digital world.".

She also pointed out that when it came to sexual offenses and domestic violence, only about 5-10% of cases were reported.

This article was originally written in German.

According to recent reports, net sales grew 2%, though demand softened in October and early November due to warmer weather, the organization remarked. Store sales increased 1%, while online sales increased 3%.

Gap also noted it's recorded a $420 million adjustment to cost of goods sold and a $21 million adjustment to interest income from tariff refunds so far this year.

It has been revealed that the company lowered its full-year net sales outlook to be "roughly flat," down from previous guidance of up between 1% and 1.5%. Gap is also now expecting adjusted earnings per share of between $2.29 and $2.34, down from an earlier expectation of between $2.35 and $2.45 per share.

Dickson said in an interview that much of the lowered guidance was due to warmer weather in the first two weeks of the quarter, but he said Gap is expecting "meaningful acceleration" in shopping ahead of the peak holiday season.

It has been revealed that at Athleta, net sales were down 14% compared with last year, coming in at $220 million. Comparable sales for the banner sank 15%, which the company attributed to "limited traction" from efforts to modernize its merchandise and marketing. `.

According to recent reports, the company's namesake brand saw 9% comparable sales growth for the quarter, with net sales of $1.1 billion, marking an 11% increase compared with last year. Dickson noted it was the brand's 12th consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales.

"Gap is really firing on all cylinders, and the consistency of the brand is really giving us confidence in the brand's ability to continue its momentum," Dickson said.

The Old Navy banner saw flat comparable sales for the quarter and net sales of $2.3 billion, up 1% compared with last year. It's the first earnings report since the brand, which has been experiencing sluggish sales, named Michael Francis as its newly introduced CEO last quarter. Francis began his role at Old Navy on Nov. 2.

Banana Republic saw its net sales sink 3% compared with last year, which the firm attributed to delayed demand for cold-weather categories and a women's fall assortment that fell flat. Wall Street had been expecting growth of 1.5%, according to StreetAccount.

Dickson mentioned the brand has since introduced fresh products and seen demand "rebound" as cooler weather has set in across the country.

Recent findings suggest that "We've been encouraged by the early customer response, and we should see sequential improvement in the fourth quarter," he said. "There's some work to do here, but with peak selling still ahead, I'm confident that the team is focused on the right areas and [will] ultimately position Banana well for growth.".

A galactic shock wave could rewrite the map of the Milky Way

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that newly introduced research suggests the Milky Way produces stars in an unexpected location, revealing a surprising difference between our galaxy and most of its neighbors.
  • The discovery comes from research led by a University of Sydney PhD student, who found evidence that a massive rotating structure of stars near the galactic center is generating powerful shock waves through surrounding clouds of gas.
  • Published in Nature Astronomy, the study also casts doubt on the nature of the Norma spiral arm, a feature of the Milky Way named for the constellation Norma as seen from Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that newly introduced research suggests the Milky Way produces stars in an unexpected location, revealing a surprising difference between our galaxy and most of its neighbors. The findings also raise questions about a familiar feature of the Milky Way, suggesting that part of what astronomers have long considered a spiral arm may actually be something else.

The discovery comes from research led by a University of Sydney PhD student, who found evidence that a massive rotating structure of stars near the galactic center is generating powerful shock waves through surrounding clouds of gas. These waves squeeze the gas together, creating conditions that allow upcoming stars to form in a region where such intense forces usually prevent their birth.

Published in Nature Astronomy, the study also casts doubt on the nature of the Norma spiral arm, a feature of the Milky Way named for the constellation Norma as seen from Earth.

Lead author Dr. Hillary Davis, who recently completed her PhD at the University of Sydney's School of Physics and Sydney Institute for Astronomy, said the research provides upcoming insights into the structures near the galactic center and how gas moves around them.

"At its heart, star formation is a process we understand from everyday physics. Forces set matter in motion. In this case gas is compressed, and that compression can create the conditions for new stars to be born on a massive scale," Dr. Davis remarked.

It has been revealed that "In most similar galaxies, star formation very commonly occurs along spiral arms. What's extraordinary is seeing this happen in a different region of our Galaxy, where shocks are usually so strong that star formation is often suppressed.".

A Hidden Star Factory at the Heart of the Milky Way.

The Milky Way belongs to a class of galaxies known as barred spiral galaxies. Unlike galaxies with only a central concentration of stars and surrounding spiral arms, these systems contain an elongated structure of stars stretching across their central region. In our galaxy, this structure is called the Galactic bar.

Sources indicate that as the bar rotates, its gravity influences nearby gas, driving it into powerful shock fronts. These fronts compress the gas in much the same way that a shock wave compresses air.

It has been revealed that studying this structure from Earth is particularly difficult because we are located inside the Milky Way rather than viewing it from the outside. Large amounts of cosmic dust also block our view of the galactic center.

"The Galactic bar cannot be easily observed because of a combination of our position in the Galaxy and dust obscuring our view," Dr. Davis said.

"As a result, the bar's properties have been highly debated.".

Industry observers note that observations of other barred galaxies have shown that these shock fronts generally inhibit the formation of new stars, even in regions containing abundant gas. The intense conditions make it difficult for the gas to collapse into stars.

However, the new findings indicate that the Milky Way may behave differently. Although it is not the only known example, our galaxy appears to belong to a relatively small group in which substantial star formation takes place along the shock fronts of the central bar.

Industry observers note that "We believe that the Milky Way's bar has star formation occurring along its shock front, which is uncommon for most bars in nearby galaxies," Dr. Davis stated.

A Milky Way Spiral Arm May Not Be What It Seems.

To investigate this unusual activity, the research team compared detailed computer simulations showing how galaxies change over billions of years with astronomical observations of regions where massive stars are forming.

A crucial part of the evidence came from masers, naturally occurring sources that emit highly concentrated microwave radiation. These emissions are associated with the formation of massive stars and operate on a principle similar to lasers, but at microwave wavelengths.

By examining the positions of these masers, the researchers uncovered a striking match between actual observations and the locations of shock fronts predicted by their simulations.

Industry observers note that "We found that masers previously associated with the Norma arm closely align with the shock front predicted by our simulations," Dr. Davis remarked. "This suggests that at least part of the so-called Norma arm may not be a spiral arm at all, but a region of star formation along the leading edge of the Galactic bar.

"This raises questions about the Galaxy's spiral structure, and the bar region of the Milky Way, which needs further investigation," she noted.

The possibility is significant because it suggests that some of the star formation previously attributed to the Norma spiral arm could instead be occurring along the central bar. If confirmed, this interpretation would change how astronomers understand the arrangement of stars and gas in that part of the Milky Way.

New Evidence Could Redraw the Milky Way's Map.

Beyond revealing an unusual location for star birth, the research also sheds light on the physical properties of the Galactic bar itself.

Astronomers have debated the structure's length, orientation, and rotation speed for decades, partly because the Milky Way's dust and our viewing position make direct measurements so challenging.

According to recent reports, "Our findings place further constraints on the size, angle and rotation speed of this central bar," Dr. Davis mentioned.

The team's analysis indicates that the bar extends approximately 4.3 kiloparsecs, equivalent to about 14,000 light-years, outward from the galactic center along its long axis. This supports a picture of the Milky Way containing a relatively long bar that rotates slowly.

In a recent development, the results illustrate how increasingly sophisticated simulations can help scientists investigate regions of our galaxy that are difficult to observe directly. By comparing models spanning billions of years with the available astronomical evidence, researchers can narrow down the possible structures and processes shaping the Milky Way.

"By comparing a newly introduced generation of large-scale computerized galaxy simulations, evolving over billions of years, against a more limited set of observations, we now have a stronger understanding of the bar and star formation processes in the Milky Way," Dr. Davis said.

The authors reported no competing interests. Research funding came from the Australian Research Council, the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation, the Swedish Research Council, the Swedish National Space Agency, the LMK Foundation and eSSENCE (Sweden).

Computing resources and data storage were provided through National Computing Infrastructure Australia, an NCRIS capability supported by the Australian Government, and LUNARC, the Centre for Scientific and Technical Computing at Lund University, Sweden.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turnaround times are improving, crew union Bectu has revealed.

But figures show numerous productions are still breaking the agreement to give crews their legally-enshrined 11-hours rest between shifts.

Recent findings suggest that figures provided to Bectu by producers body Pact demonstrated a “significant reduction” in breaking turnaround agreements on U.K. scripted productions, the union noted. Related Stories Andrew Rannells Was Told to ‘Stay Away’ From Kevin Spacey After Meeting Backstage at ‘The Book of Mormon’; He Then Sent a ‘Handwritten Letter’ ‘Asking Me on a Date’ As Russell Brand’s Begins a 10-Year Prison Sentence, Why Celebrities Fear the Power of an Exposé.

For Band 1 productions, which cost up to £1.25 million ($1.5 million) per broadcast hour, broken turnarounds have fallen from 107 hours in 2024 to 71 hours in 2025, before dropping to zero hours during the first four months of 2026.

On Band 2 productions, which cost between £1.25 million and £3 million per broadcast hour, broken turnarounds dropped from 158 hours in 2024 to 106 hours in 2025 and then to 48 hours during the first four months of 2026.

Figures are not recorded for productions in Band 3 (£3 million to £8 million per broadcast hour) or Band 4 (over £8 million).

In a recent development, earlier this year Bectu led protests outside the London headquarters of studios including Disney, Netflix and Amazon to highlight the problem. The union has also been engaging with members and raising awareness with employers to push for better scheduling practices.

Bectu is now calling for Pact to continue measuring broken turnaround figures and extend reporting to Bands 3 and 4, including low-budget features and major film productions. The union also wants figures for unscripted productions as well as for all film and TV productions in the U.K. to pledge they will adhere to turnaround times.

“These figures are extremely encouraging and show that change is possible when workers speak out and the industry listens,” noted Bectu national secretary Spencer Macdonald. “It is also positive simply that this practice is now being recorded – it indicates a recognition that there is a problem, and creates a means to measure progress.”.

Industry observers note that “Broken turnaround has long been a concern for many crew members, who have experienced the impact that insufficient rest can have on their health, wellbeing and safety. The sharp reduction across both Band 1 and Band 2 productions suggests that awareness of the concern is translating into real improvements on the ground.”.

“There is still a lot of work to do across the industry, particularly in ensuring good practice becomes embedded. But these results demonstrate the value of collective action and maintaining constant pressure about unsustainable working hours and fatigue.”.
