Archaeologists reveal a powerful Iron Age king may have been a woman

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1093 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that newly introduced archaeological research from Bournemouth University (BU) suggests that an influential Iron Age British ruler, long believed to have been a man, was actually a woman.
  • Industry observers note that verica ruled the Atrebates, a powerful tribe whose lands extended across much of what is now Hampshire and West Sussex.
  • The Roman historian Cassius Dio claimed that Verica's appeal was the reason Claudius decided to invade Britain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that newly introduced archaeological research from Bournemouth University (BU) suggests that an influential Iron Age British ruler, long believed to have been a man, was actually a woman. The ruler, known as Verica, played a pivotal role in events leading to the Roman invasion of Britain in AD 43. The findings challenge longstanding assumptions about early British history and the political influence of women during this period.

Industry observers note that verica ruled the Atrebates, a powerful tribe whose lands extended across much of what is now Hampshire and West Sussex. Around AD 40, Verica was forced from power and escaped to Rome, where the exiled ruler sought assistance from Emperor Claudius.

The Roman historian Cassius Dio claimed that Verica's appeal was the reason Claudius decided to invade Britain. If this account is accurate, Verica's actions may have helped set in motion one of the most consequential events in British history.

Ancient Evidence Challenges an Iron Age King's Identity.

Dr. Miles Russell, Director of Archaeological Fieldwork at Bournemouth University, led the research and argues that earlier historians incorrectly identified Verica as male.

"Verica is assumed to have been male because of the patriarchal mindset of 19th-century classical historians. Verica was not only critical to the special relationship between Britain and Rome in the early first century AD but was indisputably female.".

Russell points to several pieces of evidence supporting this interpretation. One is the name Verica itself, which ends in the letter "a," a feature common among female names of the time. Other prominent examples include Cartimandua, who ruled the Brigantes (in Yorkshire), and Boudica, leader of the Iceni (in Norfolk).

According to recent reports, all three rulers lived during roughly the same period. Boudica is the best known because of her rebellion against Roman rule in AD 60. However, Russell argues that Verica may have held even greater political power and influence.

Industry observers note that another key clue comes from coins issued under Verica's rule. These coins bear the Latin title "rex," traditionally translated as "king," which has contributed to the assumption that Verica was male. Russell explains that the title was not necessarily restricted to men.

"People also assume she was a 'he' because of the term 'rex' on coins, but rex is a non-gender-specific title; both male and female kings were recognized by Rome, Cleopatra of Egypt being the most famous.".

He continued: "The use of the Latin title rex on coins indicates that Verica ruled with the full authorization of the emperor.".

The artwork on Verica's coins provides another intriguing clue. Rather than depicting the masculine warriors commonly featured on coins produced by other British Iron Age rulers, Verica's coins show a figure with distinctly feminine characteristics.

"Whilst other coin-producing British Iron Age leaders portray obviously male warriors, Verica is depicted as a slender, feminine, bare-breasted figure riding on horseback.".

The Forgotten Ruler Behind Rome's Invasion of Britain.

Russell believes Verica's importance extended far beyond the ruler's identity. He argues that Verica may have been instrumental in helping Claudius successfully invade Britain.

Ancient Roman writers frequently portrayed Claudius as an ineffective emperor who was easily influenced by women and formerly enslaved people who had gained their freedom. This reputation may have shaped how historians described Verica's role in persuading him to invade.

Russell suggests that Cassius Dio's account reinforced this negative portrayal by presenting the invasion as a decision made under the influence of a woman. In reality, he argues, Verica may have been a valuable political and military ally who supplied the Romans with intelligence and practical assistance.

"The story of Claudius committing to something only because a woman told him to fits the trope of this emperor as being submissive and henpecked. In effect, Dio was saying that the campaign was undertaken solely because of the whisperings of a barbarian femme fatale. Verica's role was rather more central to the British expedition. Having her on board ensured the project was a success, as she provided tactical information and support on the ground.

Recent findings suggest that "The invasion was Claudius' great triumph -- it being the only chance he had to prove he was a successful military leader. Verica provided the excuse for regime change, and the emperor seized it.".

For Claudius, the conquest of Britain offered an opportunity to establish his reputation as a successful military commander. Verica's removal from power gave him a political justification for intervening, while the exiled ruler's knowledge of Britain may have helped the Roman forces achieve their objectives.

Could Rome's Conquest of Britain Have Been Avoided?

Although Verica was an key political figure in late Iron Age Britain, the ruler's influence has received relatively little attention compared with that of other prominent leaders.

Russell believes the archaeological evidence supports recognizing Verica as one of Britain's earliest and most significant female rulers. He also raises the possibility that the Roman invasion might never have occurred without Verica's exile and subsequent appeal to Claudius.

"We should take the archaeological evidence at face value" says Russell "and remember Verica as a female-king and one of the earliest and most vital of British female leaders. Had she not been deposed, fleeing to Claudius for military support, Rome may never have invaded Britain in the first place.".

Latest Insights Into Women in Iron Age Britain.

The findings build on earlier Bournemouth University research exploring the position of women in ancient British society.

Last year, a study involving Russell and other BU researchers uncovered evidence of a matriarchal society in Iron Age Britain. The research indicated that husbands moved into their wives' communities after marriage, suggesting that women occupied a central position in the social structure.

Together, these discoveries are prompting researchers to reconsider the influence women may have exercised in Iron Age Britain, both within their communities and in the political decisions that shaped the region's future.

Russell's research on Verica is presented in the latest book Caratacus: Great king of Britain, published by Bloomsbury in January (ISBN 9781350477902). The findings are also discussed in the latest edition of Current Archaeology.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that after a two-year journey, the Hera spacecraft is arriving at the Didymos double asteroid system, and its first images are being released to the public today (Nov.
  • Industry observers note that the European Space Agency's (ESA's ) Hera probe rolled out atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct.
  • Hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after a two-year journey, the Hera spacecraft is arriving at the Didymos double asteroid system, and its first images are being released to the public today (Nov. 25).

Industry observers note that the European Space Agency's (ESA's ) Hera probe rolled out atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Oct. 7, 2024. Its destination is the Didymos-Dimorphos asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos, a "rubble pile" asteroid, and its smaller moonlet Dimorphos. NASA slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in 2022 in the historic DART test, which confirmed that such an impact can alter the trajectory of an asteroid.

Hera arrives at Didymos today, and ESA is sharing the first close-up images from the mission in a free online livestream. ESA's livestream starts at 1:45 p.m. ET (1845 GMT) on Wednesday (Nov. 25). Watch it live here, courtesy of the European Space Agency.

At Dimorphos, Hera will inspect the wreckage caused by DART (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), humanity's first test of planetary defense. The test was designed to see if the orbit of a threatening asteroid could be altered, taking it off a potential crash course with Earth.

The DART mission succeeded, shortening Dimorphos' orbit by just over 30 minutes, showing that kinetic impacts can indeed alter the trajectories of asteroids.

Hera will now show up to the crash scene and study the impact crater left by DART and inspect any changes the collision caused. Scientists are thrilled by the prospects.

Industry observers note that "ESA's Hera mission has arrived to learn the answers we need to know," the mission's principal investigator Patrick Michel remarked in an ESA statement. "How did the impact change Dimorphos? What is the mass of the asteroid and which of its properties explain its response to DART impact?

"Hera is carrying out a thorough investigation ever of a deflected asteroid, packed with scientific firsts, to give us a complete and unbiased picture of humankind's first planetary defense test.".

ESA has already shared some of the remarkable images Hera has captured en route to Didymos, including a breathtaking image of both asteroids as Dimorphos cast its shadow on its larger companion in a deep-space double-asteroid solar eclipse.

Hera even stopped by Mars on its way to the asteroids, snapping pictures of its moon Deimos.

Hera will remain at the Didymos-Dimorphos system for months, deploying cubesats that will study the asteroids with visible and infrared light cameras and radar instruments.

Through Hera, scientists hope to refine planetary defense techniques so that, should the time ever come, humanity has options for defending itself against incoming space rocks like the one that wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago.

"Through many years of hard work our international collaboration managed to do just that, and for the very highest of intentions: to help make Earth safer," said Hera mission manager Ian Carnelli.

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that for billions of years, Earth's atmosphere contained almost no oxygen, making the planet vastly different from the world we know today.
  • Two geochemists from Chengdu University of Technology have presented this revised timeline in The Innovation.
  • Scientists have traditionally reconstructed Earth's atmospheric oxygen levels using chemical clues preserved in ancient ocean sediments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that for billions of years, Earth's atmosphere contained almost no oxygen, making the planet vastly different from the world we know today. A latest scientific analysis suggests that oxygen accumulated in the atmosphere during three major stages, while the deep oceans took much longer to catch up. In some cases, the delay stretched across hundreds of millions of years, with the final transition involving a gap of roughly 600 million years.

Two geochemists from Chengdu University of Technology have presented this revised timeline in The Innovation. Their findings challenge the traditional understanding of Earth's oxygen history by examining chemical evidence that reflects conditions in the ancient atmosphere rather than relying primarily on measurements of ocean chemistry.

Ancient Rocks Reveal a Different Oxygen Timeline.

Scientists have traditionally reconstructed Earth's atmospheric oxygen levels using chemical clues preserved in ancient ocean sediments. However, the amount of oxygen in seawater is influenced by many factors besides the atmosphere, including nutrient availability, biological productivity, ocean circulation, and the shapes of ocean basins. This makes ocean chemistry an imperfect guide to conditions in the air.

It has been revealed that the researchers instead focused on sulfate, a chemical compound that can preserve a distinctive signal from atmospheric oxygen. Reactions involving oxygen, ozone, and carbon dioxide in the atmosphere produce an unusual shortage of the oxygen isotope oxygen-17. When sulfide minerals undergo weathering, this chemical fingerprint is transferred into sulfate, which can eventually become preserved in sedimentary rocks. By examining these signatures, scientists can gain a more direct picture of how atmospheric oxygen changed over time.

According to this evidence, Earth's first major increase in oxygen occurred during the Great Oxidation Event, between 2.4 billion and 2.1 billion years ago. Atmospheric oxygen rose from less than one-millionth of today's concentration to somewhere between 0.1% and 10% of modern levels.

Industry observers note that the second major increase took place approximately 1.3 billion to 1.0 billion years ago, followed by a third between 440 million and 410 million years ago. Both occurred earlier than conventional timelines suggest.

Under this interpretation, the well-known Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic oxygenation events, traditionally dated to 800 million to 500 million years ago and 420 million to 360 million years ago, mainly reflect delayed changes in ocean oxygen levels. The oceans responded roughly 200 million and 30 million years after the corresponding atmospheric increases.

Earth's Atmosphere and Oceans Did Not Always Change Together.

Recent findings suggest that despite these major increases, oxygen remained relatively scarce throughout much of Earth's history. Models based on the isotope evidence suggest that atmospheric oxygen during the middle Proterozoic reached only about 0.1% to 1% of present-day levels.

Sources indicate that another clue comes from the fossil record of charcoal. Because charcoal formation requires atmospheric oxygen concentrations of approximately three-quarters of modern levels, its absence from older rocks suggests that oxygen remained too scarce to support widespread burning. Charcoal first appears in the geological record around 420 million years ago.

The researchers also highlight a surprising relationship between oxygen in the atmosphere and oxygen in the oceans. Over extremely long periods, the two generally increased together. However, on timescales of around a million years, they could move in opposite directions.

When additional oxygen entered the oceans, it could react with accumulated organic carbon and sulfide, consuming oxygen in the process. These reactions could reduce the amount of oxygen remaining in the atmosphere.

According to recent reports, as a result, some chemical signals previously interpreted as evidence of rising oxygen may actually record periods when atmospheric oxygen was declining. This possibility could change how scientists interpret major fluctuations in Earth's ancient oxygen record.

Oxygen-Rich Oases Existed Billions of Years Ago.

It has been revealed that the spread of oxygen through Earth's oceans was also far from uniform. The researchers describe two major sources of oxygen in seawater: oxygen produced locally by photosynthetic microorganisms and oxygen absorbed from the atmosphere.

In a recent development, the first process created isolated pockets of oxygen-rich water as early as 3 billion years ago, possibly even earlier. These small oxygenated environments existed during the Archean, when the atmosphere and most of the oceans still contained very little free oxygen.

According to recent reports, as atmospheric oxygen levels gradually increased, oxygen entering seawater from the air became more crucial. Eventually, this atmospheric supply overtook local biological production as the dominant mechanism driving widespread ocean oxygenation.

Even then, the transformation was remarkably slow. According to the proposed timeline, the deep ocean did not become fully oxygenated until approximately 410 million years ago, long after oxygen had begun accumulating in the atmosphere.

How Rising Oxygen Changed the Evolution of Life.

These findings also offer a latest perspective on the relationship between oxygen and the evolution of complex organisms.

When Earth's atmosphere contained virtually no oxygen, its absence placed a major restriction on oxygen-dependent life. During the Proterozoic, increasing oxygen availability gradually made new environments accessible, although concentrations continued to fluctuate as early animals evolved.

According to recent reports, rather than acting as a single trigger for complex life, oxygen initially provided opportunities for biological innovation. Only after the third major atmospheric increase did higher oxygen levels become a powerful force supporting greater biological complexity.

This later transformation helped create conditions favorable for larger animals, more active predators, and organisms capable of occupying deeper marine environments.

The researchers acknowledge that important uncertainties remain. The available isotope record does not capture every change in detail, and absolute atmospheric oxygen concentrations after 1 billion years ago remain difficult to establish. Additional increases or decreases may have occurred without leaving sufficiently clear chemical evidence to identify them.

Nevertheless, the analysis proposes a major revision to the sequence of events that transformed Earth into an oxygen-rich planet. Rather than the oceans becoming oxygenated first and the atmosphere following, the evidence suggests that atmospheric oxygen increased well before the deep oceans responded.

That prolonged delay may have played an important role in shaping the environments where complex life emerged and evolved.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Keep reading for the latest news and analysis from Germany on Wednesday, November 25:.
  • Bayern Munich says it has held talks with midfielder Jamal Musiala's management amid the difficulties surrounding his neurological symptoms and after comments from club management about his lucrative 2025 contract extension prompted criticism and controversy (read the backstory from Jon Harding on our sports desk here).
  • It has been revealed that "A constructive discussion took place yesterday, Tuesday, between FC Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's management," the club noted in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Keep reading for the latest news and analysis from Germany on Wednesday, November 25:.

Bayern Munich says it has held talks with midfielder Jamal Musiala's management amid the difficulties surrounding his neurological symptoms and after comments from club management about his lucrative 2025 contract extension prompted criticism and controversy (read the backstory from Jon Harding on our sports desk here).

It has been revealed that "A constructive discussion took place yesterday, Tuesday, between FC Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's management," the club noted in a statement. "For both parties, the player's health is the absolute priority. Jamal Musiala will receive full support throuhgout his recovery process.".

The club also clarified when Musiala — who collapsed twice in pre-season friendlies as a result of what he has described as "absence seizures" — first started exhibiting neurological symptoms that only became widely known with the announcement of his diagnosis at the start of this season.

"In light of various rumors circulating over the past few days, FC Bayern and 11WINS — the agency representing Jamal — wish to clarify the following: Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025," the club mentioned. "This examination took place in consultation with FC Bayern and the club's medical department, immediately following the onset of these neurological symptoms.".

In a recent development, musiala had signed a contract extension to 2030 earlier that year. Several senior Bayern officials had voiced doubts about his contractual status in recent days, saying it appeared unlikely he would be able to return to his past peak form going forward. This prompted a stern rebuke from the players' union and others.

After being sidelined with a hamstring injury in September, Musiala returned to action last week in the 1-1 draw with Cologne.

The right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) has formally put forward its leader in Saxony-Anhalt to head the eastern state's next regional government.

Given the stalemate after September's elections, with the AfD by far the largest party but still well short of a majority in its own right, it's anything by clear that Siegmund will receive the 42 votes he'd need to become state premier.

The AfD holds 39 seats in the Magdeburg parliament so Siegmund would need three votes from members of other parties in the secret ballot.

In a recent development, but what's now clear is that a vote to see if he can command a majority will go ahead, provisionally on December 8. Siegmund had mentioned last week that he planned to take this step.

"I am working on the assumption that there will only be one vote," Siegmund remarked, voicing confidence in winning the required support, even though nobody outside his party has indicated an intention to vote for him.

The left-wing populist BSW, which holds five seats, has mentioned its members intend to abstain, while 14 of 15 CDU lawmakers in the state have said they intend to leave the chamber in the first two rounds of voting.

It's not clear how the process might end as yet.

But if a candidate stands in two votes in the state parliament — which must take place within one week of each other — and cannot command a majority in either, a newly introduced vote is triggered on whether to call new elections. This must take place within two weeks. In this situation, a simple majority voting in favor would suffice to trigger another election.

If there is no majority vote for another election, then a third vote for a state government leader is triggered.

In this final round, a candidate only needs a majority of the total votes cast, not a majority of the total number of members of the chamber, in order to be elected.

In the event that even this third vote is not decisive, with a tie of votes for and against — which given the arithmetic in the parliament does seem at least to be a conceivable possibility — then Germany's written laws don't make it explicitly clear what the tie-break function would be.

Legal experts have said they believe the most likely solution would be to continue holding votes until a majority or plurality decision can be reached.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has voiced dissatisfaction with cuts to his department's 2027 funding during Wednesday's Bundestag budget debate.

He described the planned budget for his department as "responsible," albeit adding: "But to be honest, I cannot give my budget a much better evaluation than that.".

Wadephul mentioned that given the precarious geopolitical situation it was "difficult to understand" why the Foreign Ministry was not exempt from the more general savings drive.

He noted that while the Defense Ministry budget was bolstered to a large extent by the so-called "special fund" to boost defense and rearmament spending, "not a single euro cent" of that extra-budgetary financial allowance flowed to the Foreign Ministry.

The Foreign Ministry's proposed 2027 budget is smaller than this year's, but not by very much. The proposals foresee cutting it from €6.02 billion (roughly $6.58 billion) to €5.99 billion. The largest planned cut is in contributions to the UN and the international community, falling by roughly €200 million or almost a quarter of the 2026 total.

Experts in Nuremberg have successfully defused a World War II bomb not far south of the city center.

Industry observers note that the 225-kilo bomb was rendered inactive just before 2 p.m. local time (1300 GMT/UTC), city authorities mentioned in a press release.

The US bomb dropped in an air raid had been unearthed a day earlier at a construction site.

A precautionary evacuation radius of 500 meters was established to deal with the explosive, with roughly 700 residents asked to leave their homes in the hours before the operation.

"All those affected by the evacuation can now return to their homes," the city wrote.

An affected bus route was also resuming normal service, and authorities said that road closures and diversions were also being lifted.

Around 250 personnel were deployed for the operation.

Sources indicate that discoveries of unexploded ordnance from World War II are commonplace to this day in Germany. However, Nuremberg in the north of Bavaria represents a site rather further south and inland than the most common locations, which tend to be in the north and west, in easier reach of Allied bombing raids often introduced from the UK.

The heavily industrialized western Ruhr Valley region and major cities like Cologne in North Rhine-Westphalia are the most common sites for such finds.

The city of Berlin unveiled a upcoming memorial to Holocaust survivor Margot Friedländer.

A sign explaining the history of a building in Berlin where Margot Friedländer, then still known as Margot Bendheim, was forced to live by the Nazis has now been established.

The plaque was unveiled in Berlin-Kreuzberg by Green district Mayor Clara Herrmann.

It explains how Jews, including Margot, her mother and her brother, were forced to live there. The building on Skalitzer Strasse also housed forced laborers.

Margot's family was detained and sent to Auschwitz in 1943, where they were murdered. Margot escaped but was eventually sent to the Theresienstadt concentration camp.

She survived the war, after which she moved to the United States, but returned in 2009 to her former home. Up until her death last year, she was engaged in educating people about the Holocaust.

The head of the CDU lawmakers in the Bundestag, Thorstein Frei, defended the government's 2027 budget, despite it being "full of challenges.".

He said that taxation had been eased where it most benefited people and police, intelligence agencies and the military have been strengthened.

He acknowledged that the coalition "is not yet where it wants to be" and is also not blind to the fact part of the economic growth is coming from public spending, but he pointed to positive signals from the economy, such as the increasing business climate index.

Regarding the massive increase in military spending, Frei said: "We want to be strong so that, in the end, we won't have to use that strength.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Matthias Miersch, head of the SPD in the Bundestag, called for a discussion on how to make "large fortunes" better contribute to the good of everyone, including higher taxation on inheritance, a sticking point between the SPD and their conservative coalition partners.

"We need to discuss this now," Miersch said. "For us, this issue is by no means off the table; on the contrary, we are putting it on the agenda.".

"So far, we have always managed to find a solution—and we will continue to work toward that," he added, pointing to the €34 billion gap in the budget that the government managed to fill.

"On behalf of social democracy, I would like to say that we strive for compromises every single day, even within this coalition.".

Heidi Reichinnek, the head of the socialist Left Party in the Bundestag, has also commented on the government's budget, accusing the coalition of drafting a budget "at the expense of the majority.".

"Militarization and unbridled arms buildup on the one hand, brutal social cutbacks and a spree of budget cuts on the other," Reichinnek stated.

She accused the government of trying to protect the profits of the wealthy and big corporations while telling everyone else to "tighten the belt.".

The left-wing lawmaker noted a windfall tax on electricity companies would have helped people without leaving a gap in the budget, as happened with the electricity tax reduction that the coalition agreed on.

Timo Chrupalla, the co-leader of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), the largest opposition party in the Bundestag, has called the government's 2027 "a pure orgy of debt" after the coalition agreed to take €210 billion ($230 billion) in debt.

Merz would go down in the history books "as Germany's chancellor of insolvency," Chrupalla mentioned.

He attacked the government's continued funding for Ukraine while electricity costs go up in Germany, and called on the opposition lawmakers in the Green and Left parties to join the AfD in filing a constitutional challenge against the budget.

"This budget has nothing to do with seriousness," the head of the Greens in the Bundestag, Britta Haßelmann, said in remarks made during the budget debate.

She lamented a chaotic process that has been full of contradictions, including what she called "fooling around" with the electricity tax.

However, she also took aim at the AfD, calling the far-right party's stance on funding for Ukraine "shameful" and accused the party of spreading misinformation.

Germany has been Ukraine's biggest backer in Europe, incurring costs to help defend against the Russian invasion.

Despite falling support among German voters for this policy and increasing budget difficulties, Chancellor Merz defended the government's decision to keep funding Kyiv.

"Russia wants more than Ukraine," Merz noted in response to opposition parties during the 2027 budget debate.

"Anyone who fails to grasp this does not understand this world, or is pursuing entirely different aims with regard to our country's freedom, openness and liberalism," he added.

He also pointed to incidents within Germany that have been attributed to Russia, including the discovery of an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig Airport in August.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz has spoken in the Bundestag as the debate opens on the government's budget plans for 2027.

"We no longer have the money for everything," Merz said in his remarks to the German parliament.

He described the tight budget, which has to be finalized this week, as an "accurate reflection" of the "difficult situation as a country — geopolitically, technologically, and demographically" that Germany finds itself in.

"We will no longer be able to afford everything with tax revenue that we have become all too accustomed to for far too long," Merz added.

The government has €560.9 billion (around $614 billion) to spend in its core budget for 2027, but both Merz's conservative CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats, who make up the coalition government, have stressed that the budget for 2028 will be even more challenging.

The extra borrowing for defense and infrastructure, that marked a break with years of debt avoidance, "is limiting our room to maneuver in the coming years to an extent that many have not yet truly come to terms with," Merz warned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

German GDP only grew by 0.1% between July and September, according to updated data from the Federal Statistics Offices (Destatis).

This marked a downwards revision from the 0.2% that had previously been estimated.

"After Germany's economic performance was robust in the first six months of the year in the face of geopolitical crises, economic growth slowed in the third quarter," statistics chief Ruth Brand mentioned .

Despite a surprisingly good performance in the first half of the year, a slump in exports, as well as summer heatwaves and record-low water levels in rivers that hindered transportation of goods along Germany's key waterways, brought a slowdown to Europe's biggest economy.

Nevertheless, overall growth for the year is expected to reach its highest level since 2022 thanks to increased public spending on defense and infrastructure.

The former head of Israel's spy agency Mossad, David Barnea, is scheduled to take part in a breakfast meeting with members of the German parliament, the Bundestag, where he will discuss the ongoing war in the Middle East.

By his own admission, Barnea played a role in the pager attack that targeted members of Hezbollah in Lebanon in September 2024. The attack killed at least 37 people and injured some 300 others, including civilians. It has been described as a possible war crime by UN human rights chief Volker Türk.

That's why the human rights organization European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights (ECCHR) has called for Barnea's arrest, saying it filed a complaint with the Federal Prosecutor's Office.

"Germany must not provide a platform for alleged war criminals. Anyone who distributes thousands of everyday objects rigged with explosives and detonates them months later — without knowing where they will be at the time of detonation — knowingly accepts that an uncontrollable number of civilians will be injured or killed," ECCHR's Alexander Schwarz stated.

Criticism also came from the Green party, with Bundestag member Kassem Taher Saleh saying Barnea had "no place in the Bundestag," in comments to the taz, due to the allegations against him. However, his Green colleague Konstantin von Notz defended the invitation, pointing to the close cooperation between Mossad and Germany's own intelligence agency.

Neither the Israeli government nor Barnea have commented on the ECCHR complaint.

Following stops in the Ivory Coast and Ghana, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has arrived in Kenya for the final leg of his Africa tour.

Sources indicate that he is set to meet with Kenyan President William Ruto to discuss bilateral relations, including economic cooperation. Kenya is one of Germany's main partners on the African continent. Following Kenya's independence from Britain in 1963, Germany was the first country to officially recognize it.

During his stay in the Ghanaian capital Accra, where he took part in the opening of the German-African Business Summit, Steinmeier called on German companies to engage more deeply in African countries.

In Kenya, the German president is set to visit the special economic zone of Tatu City, where a special tax priveleges are attracting businesses.

Steinmeier last visited Kenya in 2020, but this trip is likely to be his last, with his term ending in March 2027.

Latest Update: The $500 billion beauty industry's 'green' ambitions are a patchwork at best. And they're falling short

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The escalating climate crisis is shifting many people’s purchasing patterns and this extends to the $500 billion dollar global beauty industry which is grappling with a range of sustainability challenges across product manufacturing, packaging and disposal.
  • 'Delay means death': We're running out of ways to adapt to the climate crisis, upcoming report demonstrates.
  • Strategy and consulting firm Simon Kucher’s Global Sustainability Study 2021 found 60% of consumers around the world rated sustainability as an important purchase criterion, and 35% were willing to pay more for sustainable products or services.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The escalating climate crisis is shifting many people’s purchasing patterns and this extends to the $500 billion dollar global beauty industry which is grappling with a range of sustainability challenges across product manufacturing, packaging and disposal.

'Delay means death': We're running out of ways to adapt to the climate crisis, upcoming report demonstrates. Here are the key takeaways.

Strategy and consulting firm Simon Kucher’s Global Sustainability Study 2021 found 60% of consumers around the world rated sustainability as an important purchase criterion, and 35% were willing to pay more for sustainable products or services.

This shift in consumer preferences has propelled many beauty brands to set environmental goals: to move away from single-use and virgin plastics, provide recyclable, reusable and refillable packaging and offer more transparency around products’ ingredients so customers can ascertain how “green” their purchase is.

Recent findings suggest that however, consumers still struggle to understand the sustainability credentials of many products, according to the British Beauty Council. This is because the industry’s clean-up efforts have been inconsistent, and fall short of making a recognizable impact in the absence of collective goal-setting, global strategy and standardized regulations.

Sources indicate that there is no international standard for the beauty industry on how much product ingredient information to share with customers — or how to do so. Brands can set their own rules and goals, giving rise to confusion and “greenwashing,” where sustainability claims are often touted but not substantiated.

Companies often use marketing language like “clean beauty” to make it seem like their products are natural, for example, when they may not actually be organic, sustainable or ethically made.

After rebranding in the West, many beauty companies are still offering to 'whiten' skin elsewhere.

According to recent reports, “The term ‘clean beauty’ has become quite dangerous. It’s used to sell more products,” according to British Beauty Council CEO Millie Kendall, who added that such buzzwords are losing traction in the UK as British customers wise up to their shortcomings. “Customers need better marketing information and certification information.”.

In a 2021 report calling on the industry to have “the courage to change” their business practices, the British Beauty Council wrote that, all too often, even natural ingredients involved in manufacturing products give way to “over-consumption, non-regenerative farming practices, pollution, waste and neglect.”.

“The only way out of this is transparency,” Kendall told CNN.

Jen Lee, chief impact officer at US-based brand Beautycounter, said she continues to see confusion over ingredients among consumers. (In 2013, the organization launched and published “The Never List,” which currently cites more than 2,800 chemicals — including heavy metals, parabens and formaldehyde — it claims to never use in its products.).

Industry observers note that “Natural vs. synthetic ingredients has been a conversation. People think natural is safer, but it’s not always the case,” Lee explained. “Natural ingredients formulated in the industry can have toxic load. Heavy metals can occur in natural components of the earth.”.

Mother loses peripheral vision from apparent exposure to mercury in beauty creams. Toxic levels in her home put family at risk, say experts.

“We used to be more natural and organic,” added Sasha Plavsic, founder of makeup brand ILIA Beauty. “What was challenging is (that) raw materials were difficult to source or would come in inconsistently or products wouldn’t perform.”.

Sources indicate that most makeup is created and molded at high temperatures, Plavsic explained. Purely organic materials often fall apart in this heat, leading to inconsistent results and subpar product performance. “Not every synthetic is bad,” Plavsic mentioned. “Sometimes, it helps create the best in class formula.”.

The industry’s plastic packaging is a particular sustainability challenge — 95% is thrown away and the vast majority is not recycled, according to the British Beauty Council.

In a recent development, the cosmetics business is the fourth biggest plastic packaging user globally — after food and beverage, industrial packaging and pharmaceuticals — and plastic is about 67% of the industry’s packaging volume, according to Vantage Market Research. Beauty giant L’Oreal used 144,430 metric tons of plastic in its packaging material in 2021, for example, according to the Ellen Macarthur Foundation (EMF). Estee Lauder Companies reported its brands produced 71,600 metric tons of plastic in product packaging that same year.

In a recent development, and only 9% of the global plastic waste is recycled, according to a report from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. The United States only recycles 4% of its plastic waste.

Single-use plastic is wreaking havoc on the planet. Here's what you can do to minimize your impact.

Many brands are trying to phase out harmful plastics from their operations and adopt post-consumer recycled (PCR) plastic. (L’Oreal has set a target of 50% PCR plastic usage by 2025, while Estee Lauder is targeting 25% “or more” PCR plastic — but both are far from achieving their targets.).

Sources indicate that “Between 60-70 major global brands have made unprecedented progress” in PCR plastic usage across industries, EMF’s Plastic Initiative Lead Sander DeFruyt told CNN. But DeFruyt stressed that PCR plastic must be adopted in conjunction with brands removing single and virgin plastics from their usage cycles to truly make a difference.

It has been revealed that however, PCR plastic is not easy to find — low recycling rates around the world mean there is limited supply. Meanwhile, demand for it is growing demand across industries, DeFruyt remarked. This competition hikes up its price, which is already higher than virgin plastic.

Hair care brand FEKKAI claims that it used up to 95% PCR content in its packaging, but pricing and supply issues posed a challenge, forcing it to at the moment aim for containers and packaging that feature at least 50% PCR in its packaging.

“PCR plastic is more expensive than stock plastic. The cost is hard and then sourcing it is too,” founder Frédéric Fekkai told CNN. “PCR is close to our heart, but there is a massive demand, so finding recycled plastic is difficult.”.

Recent findings suggest that beauty retailers plays a pivotal — and under-utilized — role, with control over stocking decisions and supply chains. But many vary when it comes to the standards they set for brands they sell.

According to recent reports, “Smaller businesses do more, full stop,” noted Jessi Baker, founder of the technology platform Provenance, which helps brands display their sustainability credentials for customers. “They move more nimbly. Some of them are born-good brands — climate friendliness was part of their setup. They don’t need to restructure their entire supply chain. Their culture already has it compared to the larger brands who need to work hard to change.”.

A history of beauty trends -- and the standards that shaped them.

Sephora debuted its “Clean + Planet Positive” initiative in 2021, which labeled products that met its set criteria. (This is separate from the French retailer’s “Clean at Sephora” program, which is at the moment facing a consumer lawsuit alleging it carries a significant percentage of products understood by customers to be harmful.) Target launched a similar program in 2022, featuring a “Target Zero” icon for both online and in-store offerings that either have reusable, recyclable, compostable or reduced plastic packaging, or feature waterless or concentrated products.

Still, many steps taken by brands and retailers do not even begin to touch on the waste and pollution generated throughout supply chains, manufacturing and shipping, all huge problems for the industry to grapple with.

Recent findings suggest that the gaps in standardization in the beauty ecosystem can, to some extent, be filled by certifications such as the US-born B Corporation, or B Corp. This accreditation, one of the most well-known in the beauty space, is issued by the non-profit B Lab, which scores a company on a variety of criteria around ethics and sustainability. However beneficial it may be among eco-conscious consumers, though, it is right now completely voluntary for brands to apply for.

Governments and multinationals enforcing regulations and setting a base line for brands to operate from when making sustainability claims would go a long way to making change, many experts and business leaders believe.

Susanne Kaufmann, founder of her namesake beauty brand, says her efforts in Austria would reap better results if more countries around the world had stricter, more uniform garbage disposal laws.

A trash heap 62 meters high highlights the scale of India's climate challenge.

“I package our product in a recyclable material,” Kaufmann stated. (Her products’ packaging, which is refillable and reusable, is made from 75% recycled plastic — and is 100% recyclable.) If I send this to the US, the garbage is not separated… and it’s not recyclable,” she explained, referring to inconsistencies in recycling laws across the United States.

Industry observers note that and when it comes to ingredients, the European Chemicals Agency lists 2,495 substances banned from use in cosmetic products marketed for sale or use in the bloc. But the US Food and Drug administration only lists 11, making it more challenging for American consumers to find safer, greener options. The Environmental Working Group, a non-profit watchdog, studied lab tests of 51 sunscreen products in 2021 and found that only 35% of products met the EU standard, compared with 94% that passed the US standard.

However, while government can set minimum requirements, Mia Davis, vice president of sustainability and impact at beauty retailer Credo Beauty, indicates the needle will move in the private sector.

Sustainable ships: The world's most eco-conscious cruises.

“Regulation can raise the floor a bit. A person who doesn’t know about any (sustainability complications) should still be able to walk into a bodega and get clean products… But that’s never going to be what the market can do,” she said. “Market leadership is key.”.

It has been revealed that in the absence of bold regulations or global standards on sustainability practices, this “leadership” — undertaken both by brands and customers in the beauty marketplace — is likely to be the most immediately impactful vector for addressing the industry’s climate shortcomings. It will take continued collective advocacy and initiative to see meaningful climate-conscious change.

Ex-GM CEO on Mary Barra succession planning: 'It's going to be tough'

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (735 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former General Motors CEO and Chairman Dan Akerson doesn't mince words when asked about the challenges the automaker faces in finding a successor for GM CEO Mary Barra: "It's going to be tough.".
  • The 78-year-old businessman and U.S.
  • Akerson said Barra will be hard to replace, citing her success and prominence as the first female CEO of any major automaker and the ongoing challenges facing the automotive industry, such as artificial intelligence, vehicle digitalization, and the rise of China and autonomous vehicles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former General Motors CEO and Chairman Dan Akerson doesn't mince words when asked about the challenges the automaker faces in finding a successor for GM CEO Mary Barra: "It's going to be tough.".

He should know. The 78-year-old businessman and U.S. Navy veteran helped with his own succession planning and recommended to GM's board in 2013 that Barra replace him as CEO. She has held the top job since Jan. 15, 2014.

Akerson said Barra will be hard to replace, citing her success and prominence as the first female CEO of any major automaker and the ongoing challenges facing the automotive industry, such as artificial intelligence, vehicle digitalization, and the rise of China and autonomous vehicles.

Industry observers note that "It's going to be very, very dynamic," Akerson told CNBC during a phone interview. "It's going to be a big change.".

Akerson declined to discuss potential internal candidates such as GM Chief Product Officer Sterling Anderson, CFO Paul Jacobson or President Mark Reuss, but he said the eventual successor needs to be dynamic and, if from the outside, "adaptable.".

According to recent reports, his comments to CNBC follow a Wall Street Journal report on Tuesday that GM is working with an executive search firm to identify possible outside candidates to succeed Barra, in addition to internal prospects. GM declined to comment on the report or Barra's succession.

Akerson, who came to GM as an outsider from The Carlyle Group in 2010, noted selecting an outside candidate might be risky if there are already executives within the organization who have similar leadership and technical expertise.

"Is there anybody in the organization that has that background that you know better day to day over a period of time? You may be taking a risk by bringing in an outsider," he stated.

The prospect of an outsider leading GM would be unusual in the auto industry, where major automakers have generally promoted internal CEO candidates, apart from periods of exceptional disruption such as the Great Recession.

Stellantis, BMW, Toyota Motor, Nissan Motor and Hyundai Motor have all appointed internal executives to their CEO positions in recent years.

Barra has noted several times that her successor and her longevity in the role would be determined by the board.

A notable influence is likely Hewlett Packard veteran Patricia Russo, GM's longest-serving board member who has been on the board since 2009 and leads its CEO succession planning as independent lead director.

GM's CEO succession planning is done "at least annually," according to the firm's yearly proxy filing. That process includes Barra providing the board "with recommendations for, and evaluations of, potential CEO successors and discusses developmental plans for these successors," according to the filing.

That is followed by board members engaging "with CEO candidates and senior management talent at Board and committee meetings and other forums to enable directors to personally assess candidates.".

When Akerson was preparing to retire, Barra was among a pool of four candidates — two longtime GM employees and two relative newcomers — who were finalists for CEO in 2013, he noted.

Akerson said he put the finalists through an extended evaluation, asking how they viewed GM's strengths and weaknesses, how they would organize the firm, and their willingness to work together, potentially with other CEO candidates who didn't get the job.

Akerson remarked the final decision to appoint Barra was done at a day-and-a-half-long board meeting in Washington. The candidate field was narrowed to Barra and former GM executive Dan Ammann, an ex-Wall Street banker who was GM's CFO before leaving the automaker's Cruise unit, reportedly over a disagreement in strategy with Barra, in 2021.

Industry observers note that "Mary's very deserving of all the accolades she's received," Akerson said. "She's done a terrific job.".

Barra has been leading the automaker for nearly 13 years, which makes her the longest-serving CEO of the automaker since Alfred Sloan retired after a 23-year career as CEO in 1946.

Akerson said he believes that, like he did, Barra will have major influence in picking her successor. He described that dynamic as integral to continuing her legacy leading the automaker.

In a recent development, "This is crucial. I think if she doesn't pick the right person, in four or five years from now and things are back in the trough, that will tarnish her history. But I think she'll pick the right one," he remarked.

#117055. Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1255 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1255 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that astronomers have identified an extraordinary pair of quasars dating back to just 900 million years after the Significant Bang.
  • It has been revealed that an international research team has discovered the most distant compact pair of quasars ever observed, offering a rare glimpse into the earliest stages of cosmic history.
  • Although astronomers believe paired quasars should be relatively common, finding and studying them is exceptionally difficult.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that astronomers have identified an extraordinary pair of quasars dating back to just 900 million years after the Significant Bang. Each is powered by an enormous black hole that somehow grew to an astonishing size when the Universe was still in its infancy. Scientists have no definitive explanation for how these two cosmic giants became so massive so rapidly. The remarkable pair has been given the Hawaiian name Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.

It has been revealed that an international research team has discovered the most distant compact pair of quasars ever observed, offering a rare glimpse into the earliest stages of cosmic history. Officially designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the pair also holds the record for the closest separation between two known quasars from the early period known as cosmic dawn.

Although astronomers believe paired quasars should be relatively common, finding and studying them is exceptionally difficult. Discovering two so close together, especially from such an early period in the Universe's history, makes this finding particularly remarkable.

The discovery was made possible by combining observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Gemini North telescope on Maunakea, a dormant volcano in Hawai'i. The research was led by Silvia Onorato, a postdoctoral research associate at NSF NOIRLab, and is described in a paper published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Sources indicate that gemini North is one of the two telescopes that make up the International Gemini Observatory. Operated by NSF NOIRLab, the observatory is an international partnership led by the U.S. National Science Foundation, with participation from Canada, Chile, Brazil, Argentina, and the Republic of Korea.

How Giant Black Holes Formed in the Early Universe.

In a recent development, during the first billion years after the Major Bang, the Universe underwent a period of extraordinary transformation. Vast concentrations of invisible matter, known as dark matter halos, collapsed under gravity. The earliest galaxies began producing stars, while increasingly massive galaxies developed the first supermassive black holes at their centers.

As galaxies passed near one another, collided, and sometimes merged, enormous quantities of gas and stars became available to feed their central black holes. Some of the material falling toward these black holes released tremendous amounts of energy. This process, known as accretion, could generate radiation so intense that the glowing region surrounding a black hole outshone every star in its host galaxy.

Astronomers call these extraordinarily luminous objects quasars.

Recent findings suggest that because galaxy encounters and mergers occur frequently throughout the Universe, researchers expect many quasars to exist in pairs separated by distances smaller than the typical diameter of a galaxy. Yet detecting these systems has remained a major challenge.

According to recent reports, one reason is that a supermassive black hole spends only a relatively brief period in its bright "quasar phase." Another is the enormous distance separating ancient quasars from Earth, which makes them appear extremely faint to ground-based telescopes. Even when both objects are visible, their close proximity can make it difficult to distinguish one from the other.

Two Monster Black Holes That Grew Too Big, Too Fast.

Sources indicate that nāpōwawāʻenakaulua stands out because it is only the third known quasar pair from cosmic dawn. More importantly, its two black holes were already so enormous at such an early stage of cosmic history that existing theories cannot definitively explain their growth.

The black holes are separated by approximately 18,100 light-years, equivalent to about one-fifth the diameter of the Milky Way. One has an estimated mass of 1.5 billion Suns, while the other weighs approximately 400 million solar masses.

Astronomers see the pair as it appeared only 900 million years after the Big Bang, when the Universe was still populated by relatively young stars, galaxies, and black holes. Finding two black holes comparable in mass to many present-day supermassive black holes at this early time raises difficult questions about how quickly the first enormous cosmic structures could assemble.

Sources indicate that "There is no definitive theoretical explanation for how a single one of these giant quasars exists so early in the age of our Universe, much less two," states Onorato. "We observed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua at a time when the Universe was only a thirteenth of its age and astonishingly, its supermassive black holes are just as massive as those we see today.".

According to recent reports, the pair's Hawaiian name reflects the extraordinary forces involved. Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua translates to "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the Universe.".

The name was developed through the A Hua He Inoa program, a collaboration involving the ʻImiloa Astronomy Center of Hawaiʻi and the University of Hawai'i's Ka Haka ʻUla O Keʻelikōlani (Hawaiian Language College).[1].

How James Webb and Gemini North Revealed the Hidden Pair.

Recent findings suggest that the discovery began with data collected by the Aether survey, a JWST research program designed to identify and characterize objects from the early Universe. The project is led by Emanuele Paolo Farina, an Associate Scientist at NSF NOIRLab/Gemini.

Recent findings suggest that using JWST's Near-Infrared Spectrograph Integral Field Unit, the survey assembled observations of 200 quasars. That sample represents approximately 43% of all quasars known from this period of cosmic history.

Sources indicate that while visually examining the survey data, researchers noticed something unexpected. A previously identified quasar, J1602+4228A, appeared to have a companion.

To investigate, the team turned to Gemini North's Gemini Near-Infrared Spectrograph (GNIRS). These observations allowed astronomers to distinguish the two quasars individually, providing crucial evidence about the nature of the system.

In a recent development, obtaining those measurements was an exceptional achievement. The objects are separated by such a small apparent distance, and the companion J1602+4228B is so faint, that resolving them with a telescope on Earth was expected to be nearly impossible.

Fortunately, the researchers benefited from exceptionally favorable observing conditions on Maunakea. Clear skies and unusually sharp atmospheric conditions enabled them to gather the necessary observations in just two nights.

"The sky over Maunakea was so clean and sharp that we managed to collect the data in only two nights," says Onorato.

The team also used Gemini North's Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph (GMOS) to gather additional information about the system and refine their understanding of the two quasars.[2].

A Upcoming Clue to the Universe's First Giant Galaxies.

Industry observers note that exactly how Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua formed remains unknown. However, the researchers believe its extraordinary properties could point to an unusually dense concentration of matter in the early Universe.

In such an environment, frequent interactions between young galaxies may have provided enormous supplies of gas, simultaneously accelerating the birth of stars and fueling rapid growth of the black holes at their centers.

If this interpretation is correct, the quasar pair could help scientists understand how the earliest massive galaxies developed alongside their central supermassive black holes.

"Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua is a really unique environment," says Onorato. "It's a laboratory for astronomers to study how the very first massive galaxies and their central black holes assembled together through direct galaxy interactions during these early times.".

  • According to recent reports, the Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.
  • In addition to food, supplies, and equipment for the crew, Cygnus will deliver several upcoming experiments aimed at improving drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis treatment, predicting cancer spread, advancing treatments for muscle loss, improving radiation sensing, and supporting food production for future long-duration missions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the manufacturer’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft.

According to recent reports, the Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following arrival to the station, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 to grapple the spacecraft before ground controllers robotically install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading.

In addition to food, supplies, and equipment for the crew, Cygnus will deliver several upcoming experiments aimed at improving drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis treatment, predicting cancer spread, advancing treatments for muscle loss, improving radiation sensing, and supporting food production for future long-duration missions. This research includes:.

It has been revealed that cardinal Muscle 2.0 uses the microgravity environment to explore potential treatments for muscle loss. Muscle atrophy and strength loss experienced by astronauts after spaceflight share many features with age-related muscle decline on Earth and occur more rapidly in microgravity without exercise. Researchers will use a muscle tissue model to test different Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs used to treat other conditions can be repurposed to prevent or reduce muscle loss.

The DNA Nano B investigation uses microgravity to manufacture tiny, DNA-inspired particles designed to deliver medicine into dense tissues, such as cartilage and solid tumors. Microgravity may enable more uniform particle assembly, helping researchers refine production methods. The results could advance targeted treatments for cancer and osteoarthritis on Earth.

The Active Radiation Environment Sensor (ARES) will test a small radiation monitoring device to support future Artemis program and lunar missions. The system is designed to integrate with spacecraft systems and provide real-time radiation monitoring inside crew living areas. The results could inform radiation monitoring strategies and crew safety measures for future exploration missions.

Encapsulate-1 uses miniature replicas of patients’ tumors to study how cancer cells move, invade surrounding tissues, and potentially spread. Researchers aim to develop a space-based diagnostic tool that could predict cancer progression months or even years in advance, improving early detection and treatment decisions for patients on Earth.

Sources indicate that ohalo III is a newly introduced plant growth facility designed to help food crop production on future long-duration missions. The mostly automated system uses innovative water recovery and air exchange technologies to grow a variety of crops. This research could help lead to better food production methods to keep crew healthy and fed on future exploration missions, including those to Mars.

JOining demonstrations IN-Space (JOINS) will mature technologies that allow robotic systems to join materials directly in space. In-space joining could enable large structures to be assembled and integrated after launch rather than being constrained by the size and volume of a launch vehicle. These capabilities may be needed to build and repair large infrastructure, such as structures that will to support future exploration under Moon Base.

Testing technologies in space helps validate their performance in unique environmental conditions, matures their readiness for operational use, reduces technical risk, and builds confidence for future mission applications.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima.
  • When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Iwo Jima looks remarkably different from space after a volcanic eruption created new land extending the Japanese island's beaches.

On Oct. 27, Japan's Meteorological Agency detected an underwater volcanic eruption off the shores of Iwo Jima. Soon after this initial detection of the "submarine" volcano, satellites orbiting our planet started taking a look, observing to see what havoc this eruption might wreak.

When you compare the satellite images above captured by the Landsat 9 satellite's Operational Land Imager (OLI), you can see the stark differences between the island on October 26 before the eruption and weeks later on November 11.

In a recent development, the island was also observed by NASA's NISAR spacecraft as well as the MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensors. Together, this imagery gave researchers a more complete picture of how the eruption continued and the effects it left behind.

And amazingly, with satellite imagery experts have been able to show that the eruption has actually added more land to the island's beaches.

On Nov. 16, Japan's Coast Guard confirmed in a statement that about 125 acres (50 hectares) of newly introduced land is now connected to the island's southeast beach following the recent volcanic eruption.

According to recent reports, this is not the first time that a volcano has created latest land. Lava and ash from a volcanic eruption can solidify and accumulate, adding land material around the volcano or to a nearby coast if it is located offshore or underwater, as we saw in this case.

But these new landforms aren't always permanent fixtures. This new addition to the island's beach could easily and swiftly be washed away by the waves, which happened on Iwo Jima just a few years ago in 2023. And experts expect the same thing to happen with this new land.

Industry observers note that "I imagine we'll see this newly introduced land wash away within a few months," Daniel Slayback, a scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center who has previously studied landforms created by volcanic eruptions, said in a statement. "But we'll have to wait and see.".

Breaking: Amateur Astronomer? Be a Kilonova Catcher!

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (483 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nasa

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, neutron stars are the ultra-dense, city-sized leftovers of dead stars.
  • It has been revealed that kilonova Catcher connects amateur astronomers around the world into a rapid-response network.
  • The Kilonova Catcher network has more than 150 registered members on several continents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, neutron stars are the ultra-dense, city-sized leftovers of dead stars. When they collide, they can release a brief flash of light called a kilonova. These immensely powerful events forge much of the universe’s gold, platinum and other heavy elements. Since a kilonova fades within days, astronomers have to find it fast, and no single observatory can watch the whole sky. But if you have a telescope with a camera, or access to one, you can help find and follow these cosmic fireworks as a part of NASA’s Kilonova Catcher project!

It has been revealed that kilonova Catcher connects amateur astronomers around the world into a rapid-response network. When gravitational wave detectors or space telescopes send out an alert, volunteers point their own telescopes at the sky to help find and track the fading light. The network also follows up on gamma-ray bursts, the most powerful explosions in the universe, and catches other short-lived cosmic events whenever the opportunity arises.

The Kilonova Catcher network has more than 150 registered members on several continents. Volunteers work side by side with professional astronomers and observatories. They have already contributed to more than 64 official reports shared through NASA’s General Coordinates Network, the system scientists use to share discoveries in real time. Volunteers’ observations have been credited for their contributions by being named authors in peer-reviewed scientific research papers. Kilonova Catcher volunteers also joined NASA’s lunar Impact Flash! project campaign during the Artemis II mission, recording the tiny flashes of light made when meteoroids strike the Moon. The network is getting ready to help follow up thousands of fresh alerts from NASA’s new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

Sources indicate that "Here at Kilonova Catcher, by chasing the light from gravitational-wave events, we’re seeing how a single collision reaches across the universe,” said Cristina Andrade, Kilonova Catcher head of operations at the Minnesota Institute for Astrophysics. “The observatories that make this possible will produce an unprecedented amount of data. We need more human minds, more people with their eyes on the sky and on the data, both literally and figuratively. And more importantly, we need more people to realize they are capable of great feats of science, regardless of their background.".

Industry observers note that the Kilonova Catcher project is co-led by Andrade and Principal Investigator Dr. Damien Turpin, a researcher at the French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA). Damien said, “I am inspired by the expertise and drive of our amateur astronomers. They are always digging for more information and pushing the limits of their understanding. This science could not be done without their contributions.”.

To register and become a Kilonova Catcher, visit https://kilonovacatcher.in2p3.fr/ or send an email to kilonovacatcher@gmail.com. Anyone who has access to a telescope with a camera can take part!

Use your backyard telescope to spot the most cataclysmic collisions in our Universe!
